questions.question: Which of these are indigenous peoples of North America?
questions.explanation: Native Americans are the indigenous peoples of the USA and Canada. The Maori live in New Zealand and Aboriginal Australians in Australia.

questions.question: What is a common historical experience shared by Native Americans, Aboriginal Australians and the Maori?
options: Colonisation, loss of land and discrimination
They all moved voluntarily to new countries
They were never affected by European settlers
They all share the same language
questions.explanation: All three indigenous peoples experienced colonisation, loss of land, discrimination and pressure on their languages and cultures.

questions.question: Which indigenous people in Norway can be compared to the indigenous peoples of the English-speaking world?
questions.explanation: The Sami are Norway's indigenous people, and their history of assimilation pressure has parallels to indigenous peoples in the USA, Australia and New Zealand.

questions.question: How is Maori culture treated in New Zealand society today?
options: It is a visible and respected part of society, with its own language and traditions
questions.explanation: Maori culture is a visible and respected part of New Zealand society, with the Maori language having official status.

questions.question: What are many indigenous communities doing today?
options: Working to revive their languages and preserve their cultures
Refusing all contact with modern society
questions.explanation: Indigenous peoples around the world actively work to revive languages, preserve traditions and gain recognition for past injustices.
